places.name: Mission San Diego de Alcalá
places.text: First of the 21 Alta California missions, founded July 16, 1769; known as the Mother of the Missions.
places.more: In November 1775 Kumeyaay fighters burned the mission; Father Luis Jayme was killed and is called California's first Christian martyr. He is buried by the altar. Today's church is the fifth on the site: a 1931 rebuild that replicates the church dedicated November 12, 1813.

places.name: Mission San Gabriel
places.text: Church completed 1805, designed by Father Antonio Cruzado with capped buttresses and tall narrow windows unlike any other mission; CMF ties the style to the cathedral of Córdoba.
places.more: The December 8, 1812 earthquake toppled the original bell tower; the six-bell campanario replaced it. An arson fire on July 11, 2020 destroyed the church roof. The campus reopened July 1, 2023 with a new museum exhibit naming 7,054 Native people baptized 1771 to 1848.

places.name: Mission San Juan Capistrano
places.text: The Serra Chapel (1782) is regarded as the oldest building in California still in use and the last standing church where Serra is known to have said Mass.
places.more: The Great Stone Church, begun 1797 and finished 1806, collapsed in the December 8, 1812 earthquake during Mass on the feast of the Immaculate Conception; about 40 worshipers died (Wikipedia adds two boys ringing the bells). The return of the swallows is celebrated each year on St. Joseph's Day, March 19.

places.name: Mission San Fernando
places.text: The church was destroyed by the 1971 San Fernando earthquake and rebuilt by 1974.
places.more: The convento, finished in 1822 after twelve years of work, has a 19-arch colonnade. Bob Hope (2003) and Dolores Hope (2011) are buried in the Bob Hope Memorial Gardens.

places.name: Mission San Luis Rey
places.text: Called the King of the Missions for its size; the mission calls itself the largest of California's missions, with 2,869 people in 1825 (CMF).
places.more: The 1815 church is the only surviving mission church built in a cross shape, with a wooden dome and cupola. California's first pepper tree, from Peru, was planted here in 1830.
